title: TrafficAlign: Aligning Large Language Models for Traffic Scenario Generation

control_signal.value: Choice of target region (one aligned LLM per region) and a prompt to the aligned LLM, which outputs natural-language traffic scenario descriptions; no fine-grained user steering shown in packet.

control_mechanism.value: Supervised fine-tuning with LoRA on scenario descriptions synthesized from driving videos by a multimodal LLM and validated via a DSL checker; the aligned LLM is then prompted to generate descriptions.

base_model.value: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct as generator (LoRA SFT); GPT-4.1 nano as video-frame scenario extractor; scenarios executed as CARLA simulations in SafeBench.

datasets.value: 261 first-person YouTube driving videos across six regions (Los Angeles, New York City, Yosemite, Yellowstone, small town in Pennsylvania, Switzerland); SafeBench platform with PPO, SAC, TD3 ego models.

metrics.value: SafeBench metrics (10 or 11): collision rate, overall score, traffic-signal adherence, route metrics, smoothness; qualitative UMAP overlap of scenario-description embeddings with real-world scenarios.

controllability_evidence.value: Alignment, not steering: scenarios raise collision rate by 2.7%-10.8% over the best baseline; fine-tuning driving models on them cuts collision rate 21.0%-36.1%; UMAP shows overlap with real-world clusters unlike unaligned LLMs.

stated_limitations.value: Uniform frame sampling may miss rare events; extractor uses a single frame per scenario and may lose temporal cues about actor behaviour.

notes: Primarily about aligning an LLM to regional traffic distributions for AV testing, not fine-grained controllable generation. Output is text descriptions, not trajectories.
